Adding a table-object adapter

Source: vignettes/articles/extending-adapters.Rmd
extending-adapters.Rmd

In Japanese

rtfreporter can read tables produced by other packages — gt, gtsummary, rtables/tern, flextable, and huxtable — and turn them into RTF while preserving their metadata (column labels, alignment, spanning headers, titles, footnotes, per-cell styles). This article shows how to teach it about a new table-object type, using the existing gt_adapter.R, rtables_adapter.R, flextable_adapter.R and huxtable_adapter.R as templates.

Read Architecture & internals first for the big picture.

The contract

An adapter has one job: convert your object into the common kwargs list that as_rtftables() consumes. Every field except data is optional.

list(
  data            = <data.frame>,   # REQUIRED: the rendered body (character cells are fine)
  col_header      = <chr vector | stacked spanning rows>,
  col_spec        = list(list(col = 1L, align = "left"), ...),
  cell_styles     = <list, one element per data row, or NULL>,
  titles_block    = <chr vector | NULL>,   # becomes the page title
  footnotes_block = <chr vector | NULL>    # becomes the page footnote
)

as_rtftables() does everything else (pagination, per-page cell_styles slicing, replicating shared metadata, attaching titles/footnotes). You do not build the rtftable yourself.

Step 1 — a detector

Add a cheap, dependency-light predicate. Keep it side-effect free.

# R/mypkg_adapter.R
.is_mypkg_tbl <- function(x) inherits(x, "mypkg_table")
# (for an S4 class use: isS4(x) && methods::is(x, "MyClass"))

Step 2 — token resolution

Tokens let users opt in/out of metadata via read =. Mirror the gt / rtables resolvers.

.MYPKG_TOKENS_ALL <- c("col_header", "alignment", "titles", "footnotes")

.resolve_mypkg_tokens <- function(read) {
  if (is.null(read) || isFALSE(read)) return(character(0))
  if (isTRUE(read))                    return(.MYPKG_TOKENS_ALL)
  if (!is.character(read))
    stop("`read` must be FALSE/TRUE or a character vector of tokens.",
         call. = FALSE)
  bad <- setdiff(read, .MYPKG_TOKENS_ALL)
  if (length(bad))
    stop("Unknown token(s): ", paste(bad, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  read
}

Step 3 — the extractor

Return the kwargs list. Always require the heavy package lazily.

.mypkg_to_rtftable_kwargs <- function(x, tokens = .MYPKG_TOKENS_ALL) {
  if (!requireNamespace("mypkg", quietly = TRUE))
    stop("Reading a mypkg table requires the `mypkg` package.", call. = FALSE)

  out <- list()
  out$data <- mypkg::as_body_data_frame(x)          # however your package exposes the body

  if ("col_header" %in% tokens)
    out$col_header <- mypkg::column_labels(x)

  if ("alignment" %in% tokens)
    out$col_spec <- lapply(seq_len(ncol(out$data)), function(j)
      list(col = j, align = mypkg::col_align(x, j)))

  if ("titles" %in% tokens)
    out$titles_block <- mypkg::title_lines(x)

  if ("footnotes" %in% tokens)
    out$footnotes_block <- mypkg::footnote_lines(x)

  out
}

Tips drawn from the existing adapters:

  • Spanning headers are a multi-row col_header: a list whose upper elements are list(col_cell(pos = c(from, to), label = ...), ...) and whose last element is the leaf-label character vector. See .extract_spanners() (gt) and .rtables_header_segments() (rtables).
  • Per-cell styles go in cell_styles: a list with one element per data row, each either NULL or list(bold=, italic=, underline=, indent_twips=) where each is a vector of length ncol with NA meaning “inherit from col_spec”.
  • Footnote marks already in the text. If your source renders marks inline (gt uses <sup>N</sup>, rtables uses {N}), convert them to rtfreporter’s ^{N} superscript markup without gsub backreferences (some locale-broken R builds drop \\1) — use regmatches() as in .convert_footnote_marks() / .convert_rtables_marks().

Step 4 — wire it into as_rtftables()

Three small edits in R/as_rtftables.R:

# (a) the list-input guard must NOT treat your object as a list of items
if (is.list(x) && !is.data.frame(x) && !isS4(x) &&
    !.is_gt_tbl(x) && !.is_gtsummary_tbl(x) &&
    !.is_rtables_tbl(x) && !.is_mypkg_tbl(x)) { ... }

# (b) the resolve-body-+-metadata dispatch
} else if (.is_mypkg_tbl(x)) {
  tokens          <- .resolve_mypkg_tokens(read)
  kw              <- .mypkg_to_rtftable_kwargs(x, tokens = tokens)
  body            <- kw$data
  cell_styles     <- kw$cell_styles
  titles_block    <- kw$titles_block
  footnotes_block <- kw$footnotes_block
}

Optionally relax the guard in as_rtftable() (the singular wrapper) so it accepts your type too.

Step 5 — declare the dependency

Add mypkg to Suggests: in DESCRIPTION. Never add it to Imports: — the zero-hard-dependency rule is deliberate. The lazy requireNamespace() in Step 3 produces a friendly error when it is missing.

Step 6 — tests and docs

  • Add tests/testthat/test-mypkg-adapter.R, wrapping every test in skip_if_not_installed("mypkg").
  • Document the new read tokens (extend ?as_rtftables).
  • Add a NEWS.md entry; for a major/minor change update CHANGELOG.md.
  • Run devtools::document(), devtools::test(), devtools::check().

A worked reference

The rtables adapter (R/rtables_adapter.R) is a compact, complete example that exercises every part of the contract — multi-level spanning headers, per-row indentation as cell_styles, inline {N} -> ^{N} mark conversion, and title/footer extraction — all from a single formatters::matrix_form() call. It is a good model to copy.
